name: Naturalisation

requirement_groups.name: Arab nationals of Oman, Qatar, or Bahrain

requirements.blocker_text: Available to Arab nationals of Oman, Qatar, or Bahrain (Nationality Law, Article 5).
Requires 3 years of continuous legal residence, legal income, good conduct, and no criminal convictions.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 3 years of continuous legal residence.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires residence in the UAE since 1940 or before, maintained continuously until the law's effective date, plus legal income, good conduct, and Arabic language proficiency (Article 7).
Requires 30 years of total residence, of which at least 20 years must be after the law's effective date, plus legal income, good conduct, and Arabic language competency (Article 8).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 30 years of total residence (20+ years post-1972).

requirements.blocker_text: A person who renders 'marvelous deeds' for the country may be granted citizenship regardless of residence duration, at government discretion.

evidence_required.document: Proof of residence history matching the qualifying category
Arabic language proficiency (general and long-term-resident categories)

sources.title: UAE Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 Concerning Nationality and Passports, Article 5: naturalisation for Arab nationals of Oman, Qatar, Bahrain after 3 years' residence
UAE Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 Concerning Nationality and Passports, Article 7: naturalisation for long-term residents present since 1940 or before
UAE Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 Concerning Nationality and Passports, Article 8: general naturalisation after 30 years' total residence (20+ years post-law)

UAE Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 Concerning Nationality and Passports, Article 9: discretionary grant for 'marvelous deeds' bypassing residence requirements; Article 11: mandatory renunciation of original nationality for all naturalised citizens

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the UAE's full build-out. The general naturalisation bar (30 years total residence) is by a wide margin the longest of any route built this entire session -- more than double Grenada's or Saint Lucia's naturalisation figures, and roughly triple Saint Kitts and Nevis' already-long 14-year Citizenship-by-Residence bar. This reflects the UAE's well-documented policy design: the country has one of the world's largest expatriate-majority populations (most estimates put non-citizens at 80%+ of residents) and deliberately makes ordinary naturalisation nearly unreachable, reserving faster paths for a narrow set of GCC-Arab neighbours (Article 5) or discretionary exceptional-merit grants (Article 9) -- see also ae_citizenship_exceptional.json for the newer, separate 2021 by-invitation program, which operates independently of this Article 9 mechanism. Article 11's renunciation requirement applies UAE-wide to naturalised citizens, hence dual_citizenship_allowed: false here -- notably NOT the case for the 2021 exceptional program, which explicitly permits dual citizenship as a stated policy change (see that route's notes).
